output.title: What seasonality can hide in a small-business workflow
output.body:
Seasonality can hide a workflow problem, not just a demand problem. If your revenue rises and falls through the year, it is easy to miss the work that keeps repeating underneath it: customer questions, invoice handling, data checks, follow-up on leads, and other tasks that never fully go away.

That is the concrete question worth asking: when business feels seasonal, what is actually seasonal, and what is simply hard to see? A task that disappears for months is usually a poor automation candidate. A task that stays in place but gets buried under busier periods is the better one to look at.

For a small business owner, the practical next step is simple. Pick one recurring workflow from the last peak season and trace it end to end: who starts it, what information it needs, where it slows down, and what counts as correct. If you cannot describe that clearly, AI is not the first fix. If you can, you have a bounded process worth testing with a human-approved step before anything else.

That is usually the part seasonality hides. The calendar changes; the same friction keeps showing up in the margins.
